_note: NPC barks. Authored from ~/Downloads/addison-npc-barks.md — hand-edited, not generated.

_schema.who: owner = the resident of this lot only. passer = somebody on the sidewalk only. any = either mouth. A stranger cannot refer to their own fence or a citation against them; a homeowner standing in their own yard cannot be walking past it.
_schema.tone: light | neutral | upset. Act I leans light; the weights shift toward upset and quiet as the campaign darkens.
_schema.needs: ALL must hold. weeds/bins/fence/junk/vehicle = that prop is on the lot. violation = any citable prop. cited = a prior FAIL or CITATION at this address. passed = a prior PASS. hot = a summer month. trashday = the day's weekday is a collection day.
_schema.tell: true means the line leaks something actionable — a grace period exceeded, a decoy flagged. Weighted up on lots where it matters, per the design note in the source doc.
_schema.wrong: true means the line is a passer-by stating an opinion that may simply be FALSE. Deliberately ungated, so 'that needs mowing' fires on compliant lawns. A player who cites on social pressure instead of measuring takes the strike, which is the lesson.
_schema._dormant: shutters, rock, repainted, pampas, mailbox, decor, gnome, twotone are not modeled yet, so lines needing them are authored but never fire. The source doc is explicit that ungated cosmetic critique of a feature that is not there reads as a bug, so they stay gated until the feature data exists.
